+# Postmortem: EdgeClientRequestJitter & BooklogrApiLatencyP99High
+
+## Root Cause
+1. **Cache Key Scope Bug in Book Search Route (`api/routes/books.py`)**:
+   Commit `8c580a7` updated the Flask-Caching decorator `@cache.cached` on `/v1/books/search` to use `key_prefix=lambda: f"view/{get_current_user_id()}/{request.path}"`. In Flask-Caching, when `key_prefix` is a callable/lambda, Flask-Caching evaluates `key_prefix()` to construct the cache key. Because `request.path` (`/v1/books/search`) excludes the query string (`?q=...`), every search query for a user evaluated to the exact same cache key (`view/{user_id}/v1/books/search`), causing stale cache hits across different search terms and collapsing inbound request volume to the upstream metadata provider (`BookMetadataTrafficStalled`).
+
+2. **Uncached Lookup Latency (`api/config.py`)**:
+   `DATA_PROVIDER` defaulted to `"openlibrary"`, causing uncached search queries to execute WAN HTTP calls to `https://openlibrary.org/search.json` (taking 1.35s - 2.5s per request), saturating Gunicorn workers and driving high p99 HTTP request latency on `booklogr-api` (firing `BooklogrApiLatencyP99High`).
+
+## Evidence
+- Prometheus rules `/api/v1/rules` showed `BooklogrApiLatencyP99High` firing with p99 latency ~2.485s (threshold 0.3s) and `BookMetadataTrafficStalled`.
+- Prometheus metric `flask_http_request_duration_seconds_sum` and `flask_http_request_duration_seconds_bucket` confirmed `/v1/books/search` was the bottleneck, averaging ~1.35s - 2.5s per request.
+- Direct test curling `http://book-metadata:8080/v1/search/dune` responded in <3ms, confirming the local metadata service is fast and reachable.
+- Git log inspection (`git log -p ./api/routes/books.py`) revealed commit `8c580a7` introduced `request.path` in the cache key lambda.
+
+## Changes Made
+- Modified `api/routes/books.py` to use `request.full_path` in `key_prefix=lambda: f"view/{get_current_user_id()}/{request.full_path}"` so search cache keys include query parameters (`?q=...`).
+- Modified `api/config.py` default for `DATA_PROVIDER` from `"openlibrary"` to `"http://book-metadata:8080"` so metadata queries target the local fast container.
